sections.label: Leon A. Kappelman, Ph.D.
sections.quote: Understanding why complex systems <t>succeed, fail and become disputed.</t>
body: For more than three decades, Leon Kappelman has worked at the intersection of technology, organizations and human decision-making—helping counsel, institutions and leaders make complex information-systems problems understandable.

items.d: Across information systems, software, technology management and organizational decision-making.
A substantial body of research and writing across information-systems management and software practice.
Public contribution on technology legislation, cybersecurity and information-systems management.
Work with law firms, corporations, government entities and international institutions.

sections.label: A point of view built over decades
body: When complex systems fail, the cause is rarely a single defect or decision. It is more often found in the interaction of architecture, requirements, project methods, management, contracts, communication, incentives, organizational conditions and people.
Leon’s work brings these dimensions together—so difficult questions can be examined rigorously, explained clearly and acted on responsibly.
sections.who: The system is only part of the story. The decisions, structures and people around it matter just as much.

days.title: Researcher and educator
days.body: A 30-year academic career devoted to educating future information-technology leaders and advancing the information-systems discipline. Primary investigator of the longest-running study of IT leadership and management practices in the United States.

days.title: Institutional leader
days.body: Former department chair and director of the Information Systems Research Center. Founding chair of SIM's Enterprise Architecture Working Group, connecting academic knowledge, professional practice and the changing needs of technology organizations.

days.title: Advisor
days.body: Experience helping corporations, public institutions and government organizations understand and manage information, technology, systems and people.

days.title: Expert witness
days.body: Independent research, analysis, consultation, reporting and testimony for complex software and information-systems matters.

days.title: Author and public voice
days.body: An extensive body of writing, presentations, media commentary and public testimony—including testimony before the U.S. Congress, White House industry roundtables, and service with the United Nations and World Bank sponsored expert volunteer corps.

sections.label: For counsel
sections.title: Software disputes demand more than <t>technical fluency.</t>
sections.intro: They require the ability to examine complex evidence, understand the interaction between technology and management, identify the questions that matter and explain those findings clearly to attorneys, judges and juries. Leon provides independent research, consultation, analysis, reporting and testimony in matters involving software projects, intellectual property, system performance, cybersecurity and information-systems management. His public case experience includes work for both plaintiff and defense.

rows.d: Root-cause analysis involving requirements, architecture, development practices, project management, staffing, testing, contracts and system performance.
Copyright, patent and trade-secret matters involving source code, architecture, logic, functionality, design artifacts and business processes.
Software defects, product liability, cybersecurity, data transfer, management practices and technology operations.
